subject: Hosted API renewal: proposed commit increase + tier adjustments
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@nimbleops.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API renewal: proposed commit increase + tier adjustments

Hi Priya —

Great speaking with you earlier. As discussed, NimbleOps is coming up for renewal on 2026-10-15 and usage has grown materially over the last 12 months. Based on the telemetry we reviewed, I recommended a path that both lowers per-token unit cost and gives you predictable throughput during your seasonal spikes.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Monthly committed throughput: move from 1M tokens/month to 4M tokens/month (stair-step, 3 months at 2.5M then full 4M).
- New rate tier pricing: blended per-token rate with a stepped discount at 2M and 4M thresholds.
- Burst window: 25% burst capacity for 72 hours per month with automatic soft-throttle if sustained.
- Rate limits: increase per-route TPS to support concurrent inference for peak collectors (we propose raising route cap from 60 TPS to 150 TPS for the primary chat route).

Attached: a draft SOW that shows the commit ladder and the revised rate card (redwood_rate_card_q3.xlsx). If this looks aligned, I can circulate an updated SOW for signature and loop in Finance/Legal for the billing cadence.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Your confirmation on the 4M target and the 3-month staircase (yes/no).
2) If yes, we’ll send an updated SOW and DocuSign link by end of week.
3) Confirm whether NimbleOps wants annual billing or quarterly invoicing with a fixed 3% financing uplift.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Priya Shah <priya@nimbleops.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@nimbleops.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal: proposed commit increase + tier adjustments

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and the call. We’re generally supportive of increasing commits — our engineering roadmap expects a sustained uptick starting November. A few clarifying questions from our side before we sign:

1) Can you confirm how the burst window interacts with rate limits? We need predictable burst behavior for scheduled scrapes. If the platform uses soft-throttle after sustained burst, will you provide latency SLOs for the first 72 hours?
2) We noticed the higher per-route TPS proposed. Will that change require code changes on our side (SDK config) or is it a server-side config we can toggle?
3) Our procurement prefers annual billing, but we need a 60-day cancellation clause tied to service degradations (not full termination). Is that acceptable?

Also — legal flagged a data retention clause in the old SOW that doesn’t match our policy. Could you remove the 18-month analytics retention and switch to 6 months?

If we can get answers on the questions above and the SOW adjusted, we can move quickly.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform, NimbleOps
priya@nimbleops.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: NimbleOps questions on SOW / burst behavior / retention — need legal/ops guidance

Team —

Forwarding NimbleOps’ reply. Quick asks from their list:
- Confirm burst behavior SLOs for initial 72-hour window and whether the soft-throttle is applied only after sustained high-percent utilization across requests.
- Confirm if increasing per-route TPS is a server-side config (ops) or if it requires SDK changes (ENG).
- Procurement asks for annual billing with a 60-day cancellation clause tied to service degradations; legal to confirm feasibility.
- Customer requests reducing analytics retention from 18 months to 6 months.

My recommended play: we accept the 6-month retention (low-risk), allow the staircase (2.5M -> 4M) but add explicit latency SLO for first 72 hours (p95 < 350ms for chat route) and make the burst policy explicit (documented burst tokens, fallback to soft-throttle when sustained >85% utilization for 40+ minutes). Also recommend we keep cancellation tied to SLA breaches (remedy window) rather than a generic 60-day cancellation right.

Kimberly — can you advise on the legal language for the cancellation clause and retention change?
Vanessa — Ops, can you confirm if the TPS increase is purely server-side and whether we need any deployment/infra work to guarantee the 150 TPS per-route? If there is cost, flag it and I’ll propose including a one-time provisioning fee in the SOW.

Thanks — need a quick turn so we don’t lose momentum.

Jonas

Original message attached below.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NimbleOps questions on SOW / burst behavior / retention — need legal/ops guidance

Jonas/Vanessa —

Quick answers so you can respond to Priya today:

1) Legal & Procurement: We can agree to annual billing with a 60-day cure/cancellation that is scoped to repeated SLA breaches (defined as 3 incidents in a 60-day window where availability < SLA and not cured within the remedy period). We will not accept a broad unilateral cancellation right. I will update the SOW language to reflect a defined breach/cure process and include a 30-day remedy window.

2) Data retention: Approved to change analytics retention from 18 months to 6 months. Please note: audit logs required for security investigations will remain 12 months unless the customer purchases extended log retention as an add-on.

3) Burst & SLO: Ops and Product agree to add a clear burst contract: a documented burst token allowance (25% of monthly commit, usable in 72-hour contiguous slices up to two times per month) with P95 latency SLO of 350ms during the first 72 hours. Soft-throttle behavior will be called out: after sustained >85% utilization for 40+ minutes, requests will enter fair-share soft-throttle to preserve cluster health.

4) TPS increase: Vanessa — if you can confirm that the change is a server-side config and whether there is a non-recurring provisioning cost, we can present that as a one-time line item in the SOW.

Jonas — once Vanessa confirms the cost (if any), update the SOW and send the DocuSign link to Priya. I’ve attached a redline for the cancellation/retention sections for your use.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
